evidence: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy shows that deposition on native oxide GaAs surfaces results in the gradual consumption of the arsenic and gallium oxides. High resolution transmission electron microscopy confirms the presence of an almost sharp interface for the 100 cycle film. Rutherford backscattering spectroscopy shows that steady-state growth comparable to that achieved on SiO2 is reached after 20 ALD cycles. Atmospheric atomic force microscopy imaging of the surface is not very conclusive as the surface may partially reoxidize in the time it takes to complete a high resolution scan.
